1.name: Cistern body
1.note: The bucket. The water between the reserve level and the float-valve shut-off level is the tokens, so its size is the capacity.

2.name: Lid
2.note: Covers the cistern and carries the pull rod through its bush.

3.name: Valve body
3.note: The fill valve's housing. Mains water enters through its shank.

4.name: Nozzle, jet
4.note: The fixed refill orifice. At mains pressure it passes the same flow whatever the level, so it is the refill rate.

5.name: Backnut
5.note: Clamps the valve body through the cistern wall.

6.name: Tank washer
6.note: Rubber washers either side of the wall that seal the valve shank.

7.name: Diaphragm
7.note: The valve's moving seal. When pressed on the jet it stops the refill.

8.name: Diaphragm cap with fork
8.note: Backs the diaphragm and gives the plunger something to press on.

9.name: Plunger
9.note: Pushed by the float arm's cam. It presses the diaphragm shut once the water reaches the full level, which is the bucket's capacity.

10.name: Pivot pin
10.note: The hinge of the float arm.

11.name: Float arm
11.note: A lever from the ball float to the plunger. It turns the water level into a shut-off.

12.name: Ball float
12.note: Rides on the water. When the level reaches the full mark it lifts the arm and shuts the refill.

13.name: Outlet shroud
13.note: Directs the jet's water into the tank, so it does not spray.

14.name: CC bolt + nut
14.note: Clamp the cistern to the pan.

15.name: Drop valve housing
15.note: The outlet fitting in the cistern floor. Its seat is where one token's worth of water leaves.

16.name: Seat washer
16.note: Seals the housing to the floor of the cistern.

17.name: Backnut
17.note: Clamps the drop valve housing through the floor.

18.name: Doughnut washer
18.note: Seals the outlet to the pan below.

19.name: Plug, overflow tube
19.note: The drop valve's plug and the overflow tube in one. Lifted by the knob it releases the dose; its top rim is the hard cap if the fill valve fails.

20.name: Plug seal
20.note: Seals the plug on its seat while the cistern fills.

21.name: Dose float
21.note: Rides on the water and lets the knob lift the plug. Below one token it rests on its stop and the pull is refused.

22.name: Stop collar
22.note: Stops the dose float at the reserve level. It marks where one token's worth of water remains.

23.name: Bridge
23.note: A yoke that couples the pull rod to the plug tube.

24.name: Pull rod
24.note: Carries the lift from the knob down to the bridge. Each pull is a request for one token.

25.name: Lid bush
25.note: Guides the pull rod through the lid.

26.name: Pull knob
26.note: What you pull to make a request. If a whole token is not there, the float is on its stop and the pull is refused.
